title: Site comparison reflects finite-Tor constructibility of bounded-below inputs
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell
e p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $T$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] and the exact comparison pullback $
u_T^*$ for $
u_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}	o T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Let $C\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ be any bounded-below complex, and let $a\le b$ be integers. Suppose that $
u_T^*C$ is bounded with intrinsically constructible cohomology [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$: its derived tensor with every degree-zero pro-etale $A$-module sheaf has cohomology only in that interval [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Then $C$ is bounded with constructible etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], and $C$ has etale Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, meaning that $C\otimes_A^L N$ has cohomology only in $[a,b]$ for every degree-zero etale $A$-module sheaf $N$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude, def-kun-derived-tensor]. No constructibility hypothesis on $C$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09AK (lemma-compare-constructible), together with the bounded-below fully faithful comparison and the finite-Tor comparison of the blueprint. Agent-explicit reflection consequence for arbitrary bounded-below inputs, not a verbatim statement of Tag 09AK.

proof.text: Put B=A_{E,n}, A=ULift B, and factor the intrinsic comparison F as the fixed-module comparison nu followed by intrinsic coefficient realization R. The Hom bijectivity in det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules gives Full and Faithful instances for nu. The coefficient realization is an exact equivalence by def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules. Hence F is faithful and exact. The existing exact-functor homology isomorphism identifies F(H^i C) with H^i(F C), and the existing faithful-exact-functor zero-reflection lemma reflects vanishing degreewise.

For each degree i, restrict the intrinsically constructible H^i(F C) to constant scalars using lem-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-module-constructibility. The homology comparison followed by the natural isomorphism of lem-sf-intrinsic-realization-origin-comparison identifies this sheaf with nu(H^i C). Apply the fixed-module sheaf-origin statement lem-weil-pbc-fixed-module-constructible-origin to obtain a constructible etale sheaf G and an isomorphism nu(G) to nu(H^i C). Full faithfulness lifts this isomorphism to G isomorphic to H^i C. Constructibility is invariant under isomorphism, and lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison translates the source predicate to the recorded finite-value etale predicate.

The intrinsic constructibility hypothesis gives a finite set S of nonzero cohomology degrees of F C. Choose a lower bound c and upper bound d of this finite set, including when it is empty. The interval [min(c,d),d] is ordered. If i is outside it and H^i(F C) were nonzero, membership in S would contradict one of the two bounds. Reflect this vanishing using step 1. Together with step 2 this is exactly the definition of bounded constructibility on the etale site.

The finite field k_0 has cardinality p^a, so has characteristic p; its algebraic closure k has the same characteristic. Since l and p are distinct primes, l is a unit in k. For every x of T, send this unit to the residue field through the canonical map k -> Gamma(T) -> kappa(x), induced by the structure morphism and evaluation. This supplies the residue-field Invertible instances required by lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude(ii). Apply that theorem with K=F C, the given bounded-below antecedent C, and the identity isomorphism, retaining precisely [a,b]. Pair its conclusion with step 3.

tool_uses.why: Exact full faithfulness on all ordinary constant-ring module sheaves is a site-comparison tool; it is essential because the etale input is not assumed constructible.
Its sheaf equivalence supplies constructible antecedents for the already constructible pro-etale cohomology; this is the finite-coefficient comparison tool used by the blueprint domain argument.
Clause (ii) is the existing same-interval reflection tool for bounded-below etale antecedents; it does not assume etale bounded constructibility and does not replace the biduality unit route.
